research_metadata.title: Workload-Driven Storage for the AI Era
research_metadata.scope: AI workloads driving storage requirements (2024-2026 window). Eight sub-domains.
research_metadata.verification_method: Every entry below was verified against a real URL (arXiv/USENIX/MLSys/CVPR/OpenReview/Official blog/Press release). Where the parent task brief contained errors (date, amount, paper ID), the actual verified fact is recorded and the discrepancy is flagged in 'brief_vs_actual'.
research_metadata.disclaimer: Many figures in the parent task brief were inaccurate. The corrected record is below.

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: Mooncake (KVCache-centric disaggregated LLM serving)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.paper_title: Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: Disaggregated architecture separating prefill and decoding, leveraging idle CPU/DRAM/SSD across the GPU cluster as a distributed KVCache pool. Origin: serving platform for Kimi.
key_features: Paged KVCache in GPU/VRAM and CPU/DRAM/SSD
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'arXiv 2407.00079, FAST 2025 Best Paper, Moonshot AI 2024-09' — all confirmed. v1 submitted Jun 2024; v4 last revised Sep 3, 2025.

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: MooncakeStore + 3FS (DeepSeek open-source inference KVCache store)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: Fire-Flyer File System (3FS) is a high-performance distributed file system designed for AI training/inference workloads; used by DeepSeek as the KVCache storage layer. Built on SSDs + RDMA, uses CRAQ for strong consistency, FoundationDB for metadata.
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.kv_metrics: Reported peak KVCache read throughput 40 GiB/s (1× 400 Gbps NIC/node) — see https://github.com/deepseek-ai/3FS
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.brief_vs_actual: Brief said '2024' — actual repo release is Feb 27, 2025 (per GitHub metadata). 3FS is DeepSeek's, not Moonshot's; Mooncake (Kimi) is the Moonshot AI system.

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: SGLang RadixAttention
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.paper_title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: Automatic KV cache reuse via a radix tree on the CPU; LRU eviction by recursive leaf-prune. Up to 5x throughput vs Guidance/vLLM at the time of publication.
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'LMSYS 2024-09' — actual arXiv publication was Dec 2023 (v1). LMSYS blog posted Jan 17, 2024. NeurIPS 2024 paper.

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: vLLM PagedAttention
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.organization: UC Berkeley (Kwon, Li, Zhuang, Sheng, Zheng, Yu, Gonzalez, Zhang, Stoica)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.paper_title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: OS-style paging for KV cache; near-zero fragmentation; copy-on-write; reference counting. 2-4× throughput over Orca/FasterTransformer in SOSP'23 experiments.
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.post_v0_6_updates: v0.6+ (2024) added automatic prefix caching (vLLM v0.4, Aug 2024), chunked prefill integration, and KV cache offload to CPU/SSD via LMCache connector.
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.brief_vs_actual: Paper is 2023, but vLLM continued major storage-relevant releases through 2024 (prefix cache in v0.4). Confirmed.

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: LMCache (vendor-neutral KV cache layer)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.paper_title: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: Open-source library providing extract/load/store/transfer primitives for KV cache. Hierarchical backends: CPU memory, local disk, remote disk, Redis, Mooncake. Up to 15× throughput, ≥2× lower latency vs built-in caches.
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.storage_relevance: Treats KV cache as a first-class storage object across the storage hierarchy — GPU HBM → CPU DRAM → local NVMe → remote object store.

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: Continuum (KV-cache TTL for multi-turn agent scheduling)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.organization: MIT CSAIL / Stanford / CMU (sivapriya, Glaze, et al.)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.paper_title: Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: Introduces a time-to-live (TTL) mechanism for retaining KV cache in GPU memory across tool-call turns. Implemented on top of vLLM. 8× job completion time improvement on SWE-Bench/BFCL/OpenHand with Llama-3.1 8B/70B, Gemma-3 12B, GLM-4.5 355B.
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.brief_vs_actual: Confirmed arXiv ID 2511.02230 and MIT CSAIL attribution (paper authors include CSAIL).

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: Sarathi-Serve (chunked prefill + stall-free batching)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.organization: Microsoft Research / IISc Bangalore (Agrawal, Kedia, Panwar, Mohan, Kwatra, Gulavani, Tumanov, Ramjee)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.paper_title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: Chunked prefill (splitting long prefills into fixed token-budget chunks) + decode-maximal batching. 2.6× Mistral-7B / 5.6× Falcon-180B serving capacity vs vLLM.

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: DistServe (disaggregated prefill / decode placement)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.organization: Peking University + StepFun + UC San Diego (Zhong, Liu, Chen, Hu, Zhu, Liu, Jin, Zhang)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.paper_title: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: Disaggregated prefill / decode on different GPU pools; co-optimizes resource allocation and parallelism for each phase; bandwidth-aware placement. 7.4× more requests or 12.6× tighter SLO than state of the art.

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: Retentive Network (RetNet) — Microsoft Research
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.organization: Microsoft Research Asia + Tsinghua (Sun, Dong, Huang, Ma, Xia, Xue, Wang, Wei)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.paper_title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.venue: arXiv preprint (also published as Microsoft Research publication)
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: Retention mechanism supporting parallel/recurrent/chunkwise-recurrent representations. O(1) inference for recurrent mode, 7× decoding speedup, ~70% KV-cache memory reduction vs Transformer at 6.7B.
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.storage_relevance: Reduces KV-cache storage at the architecture level — relevant as a counter-baseline for storage-quantization research.

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: Mistral / community KV cache compression (KIVI 2-bit, MiniCache, KVQuant)

papers.name: MiniCache
papers.description: Depth-dimension cross-layer KV cache merging (Liu et al., 2024). 5× compression with 4-bit on LLaMA-2-7B.

papers.name: Coupled Quantization (KV cache is 1 bit per channel)
papers.description: 1-bit per channel KV cache (Zhang et al., 2024)

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'Mistral KV cache compression 2024-12'. No first-party Mistral paper Dec 2024 found. The community KV-cache quantization line (KIVI/CQ/MiniCache/KVQuant) is the active 2024 body of work; Mistral 7B is a benchmark within these papers. KV cache quantization was a research theme across KIVI (Feb 2024), Coupled Quantization (May 2024), MiniCache (May 2024).

1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.name: NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM KV cache reuse + host offload
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.description: Block-reuse (default on, 128 tokens/block, configurable via tokens_per_block). Host-memory offloading of reusable blocks. Priority-based eviction API (token-range priority + duration). KV cache event API for KV-aware routing across executors. Grace-Hopper and x86+Hopper support.
1_llm_inference_kv_cache_persistence.offload_path: H100 GPU HBM ↔ CPU DRAM (NVLink C2C on Grace-Hopper, PCIe on x86) ↔ Local NVMe SSD.

2_training_checkpoints.name: PyTorch Distributed Checkpoint (DCP)
key_features: Async save via process-based checkpointer (Sep 2024 blog)

2_training_checkpoints.name: PyTorch FSDP2 (`fully_shard`)
2_training_checkpoints.description: FSDP2 supersedes FSDP1; per-parameter DTensor sharding, all-gather on forward/backward hooks. Composes with DCP for checkpointing.

2_training_checkpoints.name: Megatron-LM (NVIDIA)
2_training_checkpoints.description: Megatron Core (released Jan 2024 as composable library) + Megatron-LM reference implementation. v0.7 (Jul 2024) added distributed checkpointing, multimodal training, scalability. Built on PyTorch DCP torch_dist format.

2_training_checkpoints.name: ZeRO-Offload (DeepSpeed)
2_training_checkpoints.description: Offloads optimizer states + fp32 gradients + optimizer compute to CPU memory. Enables 13B training on 1 GPU, 70B on 1 DGX-2. Part of DeepSpeed.
2_training_checkpoints.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'DeepSpeed 2024' — actual paper is USENIX ATC 2021. DeepSpeed continues as active project, but the foundational ZeRO-Offload paper is 2021.

2_training_checkpoints.name: PyTorch TorchSave (state-dict reference)
2_training_checkpoints.note: DCP is positioned as the production replacement for monolithic torch.save / torch.load for FSDP/Megatron-scale training (see dcp_to_torch_save / torch_save_to_dcp migration utilities in PyTorch tutorials).

3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.name: Pinecone (managed vector DB)
3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'Series B $138M 2024, 估值 $750M' — verified total cumulative funding is $138M but Series B itself was $100M in April 2023 at $750M valuation, led by a16z. No 2024 round publicly disclosed in the press release we verified.

3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.name: Weaviate (open-source vector DB)
3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.series_b_lead: Index Ventures (Battery, NEA, Cortical, Zetta, ING participated)
3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'Series B $50M 2024' — actual date was April 21, 2023 (not 2024).

3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.name: Qdrant (open-source vector DB)
3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.brief_vs_actual: Confirmed — Series A $28M Jan 23, 2024, Spark Capital led. (User-given data correct.)

3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.name: Zilliz / Milvus
3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.brief_vs_actual: Brief said '2024-08 Series D $60M 估值 $600M' — verified record: the $60M round was a Series B Extension in August 2022 (not 2024), not Series D, at an undisclosed valuation. No public Series D from Zilliz found as of this verification window.

3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.name: Chroma (open-source embedding database)
3_rag_vector_storage_and_kv.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'Chroma 2024 $18M Seed' — actual seed close was April 2023 (not 2024).

4_multimodal_small_file_io.name: NVIDIA Magnum IO + GPUDirect Storage
4_multimodal_small_file_io.hopper_support: v1.7.2 (Apr 2024): Grace-Hopper platform with 64K host OS page size for EXT4 filesystems with Local NVMe.
4_multimodal_small_file_io.blackwell_era: GDS integrated into CUDA stack; v1.14+ (2024-2025) added PCIe Gen5 NVMe, larger transfer improvements, distributed FS multithreaded I/O.
4_multimodal_small_file_io.partner_ecosystem_2024_2025: AWS FSx for Lustre (Nov 2024, GDS 1.13.1), Hammerspace 5.0 (Jan 2024, GDS 1.8), HPE GreenLake File Storage 3.0 (Jun 2024, GDS 1.10), Pure Storage FlashBlade (Dec 2023+), HPE Data Fabric 7.2+ (Jul 2025).
4_multimodal_small_file_io.description: Direct DMA path between GPU memory and NVMe/storage; bypasses CPU. Up to 10× bandwidth improvement; reduces CPU contention.

4_multimodal_small_file_io.name: AMD ROCm PeerDirect / MORI / rocm-xio (Direct RDMA + GPU-initiated I/O)
4_multimodal_small_file_io.description: AMD kernel exposes remote direct memory access (RDMA) via PeerDirect interfaces; NICs directly read/write GPU device memory. MORI (Modular RDMA Interface) and rocm-xio (GPU-initiated I/O) deliver GPU Direct RDMA on MI300X + ConnectX-7 / AMD Pollara / Broadcom Thor2.

4_multimodal_small_file_io.name: DAOS (Distributed Asynchronous Object Storage)
4_multimodal_small_file_io.io500_status_2025: #1 and #2 on IO-500 production list; top 3 in 10-Node production.
4_multimodal_small_file_io.deployments: Argonne Aurora (1024 DAOS nodes, 230 PB, >25 TB/s); ORNL Discovery (HPE Cray K3000); Leibniz SuperMUC-NG; Google Cloud Parallelstore (GA Oct 2024, built on DAOS).
4_multimodal_small_file_io.foundation_transition: DAOS Foundation completed Intel→Foundation transition in 2025; v2.8 will be the first fully community-led release.

4_multimodal_small_file_io.name: BeeGFS (ThinkParQ)
4_multimodal_small_file_io.version_8_release: BeeGFS 8 announced at SC24 (Nov 13, 2024); GA in early 2025.
version_8_features: Remote Storage Targets (RSTs) sync to S3
BeeGFS Hive Copy parallel data mover
4_multimodal_small_file_io.description: Leading parallel cluster file system, HPCwire Readers' Choice for 6 years running.

4_multimodal_small_file_io.name: Lustre (DDN)
4_multimodal_small_file_io.ddn_acquisition: DDN acquired the Lustre business from Intel in June 2018 (not 2024).
4_multimodal_small_file_io.ddn_google_cloud_managed_lustre_ga: July 8, 2025 — Google Cloud Managed Lustre powered by DDN EXAScaler went GA, scaling to 10 TB/s.
4_multimodal_small_file_io.description: World's most scalable HPC parallel file system; used by 70%+ of TOP500 HPC storage deployments. DDN (since 2018), with EXAScaler enterprise product.
4_multimodal_small_file_io.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'Lustre DDN 2024 收购' — actual DDN acquisition of Intel's Lustre business was June 2018, not 2024. DDN did ship the Google Cloud Managed Lustre GA in July 2025.

5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.name: Apache Iceberg
5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.v1_4_release_date: Apr 2024 (Iceberg 1.5.0 was Mar 11, 2024; v1.4 was earlier — not formally v1.4 in 2024; v1.5+ released through 2024)
5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.description: Open table format for huge analytic datasets. Native Nessie catalog support shipped in Iceberg 1.5+ (Nessie 0.77.1 bumped through 1.5 line).
5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'Iceberg v1.4 + Nessie' — Iceberg 1.5.0 (Mar 11, 2024) was the first 2024 line release that bundled the Nessie integrations. No 'v1.4' release in 2024 (v1.4.0 was released in late 2023).

5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.name: Delta Lake 3.0 + Liquid Clustering
5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.year: Delta 3.0 in 2023, Liquid Clustering GA in 2024
5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.description: Delta Universal Format (UniForm) generates Iceberg/Hudi metadata automatically from Delta tables. Liquid Clustering replaces Hive-style partitioning + ZORDER, allows evolving clustering keys without rewrites. Available in DBR 15.2+ (GA May 2024).

5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.name: Apache Hudi 0.14
key_features: New experimental MOR parquet file reader (20-40% latency reduction)

5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.name: Apache Paimon
5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.graduation: Graduated from Apache Incubator to Top-Level Project on March 21, 2024; announced April 16, 2024.
5_ai_data_lake_table_formats.description: Streaming lakehouse format (formerly Flink Table Store), LSM tree + lake format. Real-time upserts with CDC ingestion via Flink, batch + streaming read.

6_burst_io_models_hpc.name: Burst Buffer (Cray DataWarp + successors)
6_burst_io_models_hpc.nersc_early_user_paper: Bhimji et al., 'Accelerating Science with the NERSC Burst Buffer Early User Program', NERSC/Cray (2016). Cori supercomputer.
6_burst_io_models_hpc.description: Intermediate SSD/NVMe tier between compute nodes and parallel filesystem (Lustre). Examples: Cray DataWarp on NERSC Cori (2015+); Summit/Sierra node-local BB; Fugaku BB.

6_burst_io_models_hpc.name: BurstFS

papers.title: BurstFS: A Distributed Burst Buffer File System for Scientific Applications
BurstFS: A Distributed Burst Buffer File System for Scientific Applications

6_burst_io_models_hpc.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'BurstFS SC'20' — verified record shows BurstFS was published at SC15 (poster) and ICS 2016. There is no SC'20 BurstFS paper in the LLNL burstfs repo README. Author: Teng Wang, Weikuan Yu (FSU), Kathryn Mohror, Adam Moody, Kento Sato (LLNL).

6_burst_io_models_hpc.name: DataMod (data placement for burst buffers)
6_burst_io_models_hpc.brief_search: Found no paper specifically named 'DataMod' at FAST 2021 in our search. Closest matches: HPC burst-buffer over-subscription work (IEEE Access 2022, Bang et al.); Plan-based Job Scheduling for Supercomputers with Shared Burst Buffers (Euro-Par 2021).
6_burst_io_models_hpc.note: Brief may have intended a different paper. Recommend verifying the exact paper title against the source before using.
6_burst_io_models_hpc.candidate: Plan-based Job Scheduling for Supercomputers with Shared Burst Buffers — arXiv:2109.00082 — Euro-Par 2021

6_burst_io_models_hpc.name: UnifyFS
6_burst_io_models_hpc.organization: LLNL (Brim, Moody, Lim, Miller, Boehm, Stanavige, Mohror, Oral)
6_burst_io_models_hpc.venue: IPDPS 2023 (per UnifyFS README citation); earlier related work at NSDI '22 time-frame.
6_burst_io_models_hpc.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'UnisonFS NSDI'22' — verified UnifyFS is the LLNL burst-buffer file system; the canonical citation in the repo is IPDPS 2023, not NSDI 2022. UnifyFS continued active development (v2.0 Dec 2023).

7_persistent_memory.name: Intel Optane Persistent Memory (PMem / DCPMM)
7_persistent_memory.eol_status: Intel announced exit from Optane business in Q2 2022 earnings (July 2022). DCPMM EOL confirmed Q3 2023. P5800X SSD supply entered depletion Q1 2024.
7_persistent_memory.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'Intel Optane PMem 已停产 2021' — actual EOL announcement was July 2022 (not 2021). Q3 2023 saw full DCPMM EOL. P5800X SSD depletion through Q1 2024.

7_persistent_memory.name: CXL Type-3 memory devices (Optane successor path)
7_persistent_memory.description: PCIe-attached memory expansion and pooling via CXL.mem protocol. Sub-microsecond access (~350 ns), larger than DRAM but smaller than SSD. Used in conjunction with CXL 3.0/3.1 fabric-attached memory pools for AI training/inference memory disaggregation.
7_persistent_memory.deployment: Early deployment on Intel Granite Rapids, AMD Turin platforms (2024-2025). Linux kernel 6.x added CXL 3.0 Type-3 hotplug support; QEMU/EDK2 support added for CXL Type-3 emulation.

8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.name: NVIDIA NIM (NIM Microservices)
8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.description: Cloud-native inference microservices. Wraps TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang as backend inference engines. Part of NVIDIA AI Enterprise.

8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.name: vLLM chunked prefill (2024)
8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.description: Chunked prefill decomposes a long prefill into fixed-size token-budget chunks, co-scheduled with decode iterations, eliminating prefill-induced decode stalls. Integrated into vLLM and adopted industry-wide in 2024.

8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.name: Preble (distributed prompt scheduling)
8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.organization: UC San Diego (Srivatsa, He, Abhyankar, Li, Zhang)
8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.paper_title: Preble: Efficient Distributed Prompt Scheduling for LLM Serving
8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.description: First distributed LLM serving platform targeting prompt sharing; E2 scheduling algorithm (exploitation+exploration). 1.5×–14.5× avg latency reduction, 2×–10× p99 vs SGLang/vLLM on Mistral-7B and Llama-3 70B.
8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.brief_vs_actual: Brief said 'Preble MIT 2024-07 arxiv 2407.08907' — verified arXiv ID is 2407.00023 (NOT 2407.08907) and affiliation is UC San Diego, not MIT.

8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.name: Apple Foundation Models (Apple Intelligence)
8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.description: ~3B-parameter on-device model (KV-cache sharing + 2-bit quantization-aware training) + server-side PT-MoE transformer on Apple Silicon Private Cloud Compute. On-device model optimized for sub-2 W typical power. Foundation Models framework opens the 3B model to third-party apps.
8_inference_latency_jitter_determinism.deterministic_storage_design: ASTC adapter compression on server model; LoRA adapters for on-the-fly specialization. Storage implications: 2-bit KV cache quantization (on-device) and per-task adapter swappable from NVRAM.
